H6SC01342.name: Bill Reeside Jr.
H6SC01342.bio: Retired nuclear engineer with more than 40 years in the power and research industries who later worked with Habitat for Humanity of York County.

positions.stance: Without touching benefits for current recipients, would extend eligibility ages to stabilize Social Security and personalize it for future generations.
Would replace asylum and Temporary Protected Status with "unlimited, free work visas" for low- and high-skilled workers and negotiate a path to citizenship for Dreamers.
Would extend Medicare's eligibility age without reducing current benefits, shift Medicare toward Health Savings Accounts, and return health care to a "fee for service" model.
"I will legislate for and fund the most effective and strong military in the world" but "will rarely vote to use it."
Advocates restoring private student lending and taking the federal government out of the system, while supporting trade schools and certificate programs.

H6SC04197.name: Jessica Ethridge
H6SC04197.bio: Legal professional with nearly 20 years of experience in compliance, real estate, human resources and title insurance; 2022 Libertarian nominee for Lieutenant Governor.

positions.stance: Will fight to cut wasteful federal spending, reduce inflation-driving policies, and remove regulations that drive up costs for families and small businesses.
"I will fight for a foreign policy focused on peace, accountability, and putting Americans first."
Calls the national debt the greatest threat to sovereignty and will work to eliminate wasteful spending and reduce the debt.

H2LA02305.name: Lisa Ballay
H2LA02305.bio: Nurse with more than 25 years in health care who serves as Senior Director of Surgical Services.

positions.stance: Wants more competition, less administrative burden, and visible prices for care and prescriptions rather than more federal bureaucracy.
Would target government costs and barriers that push prices up and open competition in markets where Louisiana families have too few choices.
Says permanent federal price controls don't make risk disappear; would go after what actually drives premiums.
"Protect access. Demand responsible administration." Would oppose approaches that shift costs onto patients or leave people without access to a doctor.
Supports responsible administration and accountability in SNAP.

wiki:walker-beach.name: Walker Beach
wiki:walker-beach.bio: Paramedic with decades of service and co-founder of EMS REFORM.

positions.stance: Recognize EMS as essential health care, increase support for EMT and paramedic recruitment and retention, and invest in emergency response infrastructure.
Fight for competitive pay and civil service protections for EMTs and paramedics.
Would end ambulance monopolies, protect patient choice in ambulance services, and promote competition and transparency in emergency medical transportation.
Advocate for policies improving emergency care and public safety and deliver "practical solutions instead of partisan politics."

H2LA03105.name: Tia LeBrun
H2LA03105.bio: Educator and Teacher of the Year honoree from Terrebonne Parish who holds a master's degree from UNO.

positions.stance: Secure the border with modern technology, process asylum cases faster, protect Dreamers, and create a pathway to legal status for long-term residents who pass background checks.
Supports universal access to high-quality preschool and expanded childcare assistance for working families.
Increase teacher pay through federal-state partnerships, reduce reliance on standardized testing, and expand career and technical education.
Supports two years of tuition-free community college, expanded Pell Grants, and more support for apprenticeships and skilled trades.
Defend healthcare access, protect voting rights, and preserve privacy rights and individual liberty.

H6KY04205.name: Jeremy Todd
H6KY04205.bio: Business leader who has managed teams ranging from a handful of employees to more than 300 people.

positions.stance: Will work to "end the permanent War State," reduce empire-building abroad, and stop reinstatement of the draft while keeping a strong defense.
Fully supports the plain language of the Second Amendment: "shall not be infringed."
Opposes any government censorship apparatus and government coordination with corporations or media to shape public opinion.
Calls affordability his top priority; would cut spending, shrink the debt, and "cut and ultimately eliminate income taxes."
Wants to remove government regulation, licensing barriers, and taxation that he says hold back innovation and free trade.
"We had no business entering this war in the first place"; focused on ending the war and bringing troops home.
Says Congress must hold a recorded vote before war; "I would vote NO to continuing an unauthorized war without a clear end."
Will support stronger border enforcement, faster lawful immigration, and firm action against cartels and traffickers while protecting due process.
Will fight wasteful spending, protect Social Security and Medicare, and support policies that lower the cost of living.
"I will oppose benefit cuts and another increase in the retirement age."
Proposes a Resilient Community Corps and making federal funding for environmental projects contingent on a Community Development Agreement.
Embraces Franklin Roosevelt's Economic Bill of Rights to guarantee everyone a job sufficient to afford a decent life.
Supports the Medicare for All Act of 2025 to guarantee health care for all and save rural hospitals in eastern Kentucky.
Says it is time to stop ever-increasing wealth inequality and "return wealth to workers."
Wants a government not corrupted by large private donations, PACs, influence-peddling, or bribery.

H6KY06234.name: Jay J. Bowman
H6KY06234.bio: Small business owner who has worked in construction, hybrid technology, AI power electronics and satellite thruster design.

positions.stance: Supports taxing large corporations equal to the public benefits their full-time workers receive, and strengthening workers' collective bargaining.
Supports community veto power over large data centers, a moratorium on new builds, and requiring data centers to pay for roads, water and power lines.
Proposes a universal single-payer healthcare system covering essential services, phased in gradually.
Prioritize strategic defense spending, modernize equipment, reduce waste, and work with allies to reduce the burden on the U.S. military.
Wants Congress to reverse course on tariffs to protect farmers and to pass the 2026 Farm Bill.

H6KY06242.name: Pete Lynch
H6KY06242.bio: Political science lecturer at the University of Kentucky who holds a PhD in American politics.

positions.stance: Would tax election spending above $2,500 per donor per year at 100%, ban unlimited super PAC donations, and ban congressional stock trading.
Calls for a moratorium on new data centers and requiring them to pay full grid-upgrade costs and win local community approval.
Supports Medicare for All: "Healthcare is a human right, not a privilege."
Would ban foreign and hedge fund ownership of single-family homes and cap rent increases on corporate-owned rentals.
Would break up monopolies, pass the PRO Act or repeal Taft-Hartley, and cap CEO pay at 10 times average worker pay.

H4OR04141.name: Justin Filip
H4OR04141.bio: University of Oregon graduate who serves as Secretary of the Pacific Green Party.

positions.stance: Supports diplomacy over continuous wars and reducing military spending by 50 to 75 percent.
Supports tuition-free pre-K and higher education, abolishing student debt, and a $25 per hour minimum wage.
Calls for declaring a national climate emergency, a Real Green New Deal, and banning fracking and fossil fuel subsidies.
Supports guaranteed paid sick leave, paid vacation and parental leave, plus a Federal Jobs Guarantee.
Supports banning private prisons, abolishing the death penalty, and ending qualified immunity.
Wants one searchable public database of congressional financial disclosures, faster posting, and penalties that matter.
Would restore independent enforcement with power to demand records, question witnesses, and bring cases against officials.
Plans bills to make lobbying disclosure real by exposing who is pressuring representatives and what they want.
Supports protecting whistleblowers so they can report wrongdoing safely, and punishing retaliation "every time."
Supports real, externally enforced ethics rules for Supreme Court Justices.

H6IA01213.name: Michael Bridgford
H6IA01213.bio: Small business owner raised on a family farm who interned at John Deere and earned an MBA from Northwestern.

positions.stance: "Represent the People of Our District, Not Party Bosses and Special Interests."
"Address Our Affordability Crisis by Establishing Fiscal Responsibility."
Supports term limits, a congressional stock trading ban, and campaign finance reform.
"Fix Social Security Before It's Too Late."
"Root Out the Endless Corruption in Washington and Abstain from Clickbait Politics."

H6IA02260.name: Dave Bushaw
H6IA02260.bio: First-generation farmland owner and folk and labor musician who trains workers to organize.

positions.stance: Would abolish premiums, co-payments and deductibles in favor of a payroll-tax-funded universal Medicare for All program.
Supports penalties for employers that violate workers' rights, ending "Right to Work," and labor protections for farm workers.
Supports expanding early learning and Head Start programs for working families.
Would create national citizen ballot referendums so Americans can decide issues directly.
Seeks an independent audit of $350 billion in American Rescue Plan state and local recovery spending.

H4AR01085.name: Steve Parsons
H4AR01085.bio: Retired economic consultant with a Ph.D. in economics who taught the Economics of Technology at Washington University in St. Louis.

positions.stance: Would cut inflation by ending the war in Iran, eliminating tariffs, cutting regulations and federal spending, and limiting Federal Reserve money creation.
Would end federal safety-net programs for non-citizens, speed green cards and work visas, and create a clearer path to residency for long-time immigrants.
Says Congress has "an ethical responsibility" to avoid cutting Social Security benefits and work toward a long-term fix.
Favors substance-abuse and mental health treatment over incarceration for victimless non-violent crimes.
Wants the U.S. to stop being "the World Charity and World Police," citing aid to 169 countries and over 750 bases abroad.

H4AR03081.name: Bobby Wilson
H4AR03081.bio: Manages a trim company in Northwest Arkansas that supplies home builders.

positions.stance: No automatic inflation raises for agencies; Congress should pass its 12 spending bills on time with recorded votes.
Would protect current seniors and make Congress publicly vote on real options for younger workers before the 2032 deadline.
Stop federal subsidies that draw migrants, close asylum loopholes, secure the border, deport criminals, and bar masked federal agents.
"Let people build." Cut the rules and delays that drive up the cost of a home.
Police should need a warrant to use camera data like Flock.

H6MS02188.name: Bennie Foster
H6MS02188.bio: Educator who has worked in both public and private school systems.

positions.stance: Eliminate financial waste, prioritize students, parents and teachers, and connect students with career paths as early as middle school.
Connect small businesses, entrepreneurs and workforce initiatives with available resources and funding to attract investment.
Wants to end food, maternal health and mental health "deserts" by attracting markets, mobile health centers and health professionals.
Promote government transparency, eliminate fraud, waste and abuse, and reject "spending billions on foreign aid and wars."
Believes tax money for a child's education "should be well accounted for and follow the student."

H6MS03236.name: Erik Kiehle
H6MS03236.bio: Property management businessman, volunteer firefighter for two Lauderdale County departments, and private pilot.

H6MS04259.name: Carl Boyanton
H6MS04259.bio: Businessman who founded Farmer Fresh Produce, which grew to around 100 employees.

positions.stance: Says voters have been sold "a false choice" between two parties that "protect the status quo, silence outsiders."
Says he is outraged by fraud, waste and abuse that cost the federal government hundreds of billions of dollars a year.
Concerned about runaway federal spending and a national debt over $38.5 trillion, which he calls "unsustainable."
"I proudly stand as a pro-life advocate"; says abortion should be prohibited "in all but the most exceptional circumstances."
Committed to securing borders and reforming immigration "in a way that puts American citizens and legal residents first."
